learning_outcomes.text: Master calculations on complex fluid installations.

Acquire knowledge in subjects related to energy production, both conventional and renewable, enabling them to learn new methods and theories, and providing them with versatility to adapt to new situations.
Acquire knowledge and skills for the calculation, use, and maintenance of fluid machines.

syllabus_topics: Components of a hydroelectric power plant.
Characteristic curves of a centrifugal pump (workshop practice)

assessment_methods.method: Long-answer and short-duration tests for evaluation
Practical sessions and experimental work reports

assessment_rules: For the ordinary exam, if the written test score is 4/10 or higher, the final grade is calculated as 70% from the written test and 30% from assignments and practicals. If the written test score is below 4/10, but the weighted sum is 5.0 or higher, the final grade recorded is 4.8 (fail). The extraordinary exam covers all course material, and to pass, the weighted sum of 70% from the exam and 30% from assignments and practicals must be 5/10 or higher. Students who did not attend either exam will be marked as 'not presented'; otherwise, the grade recorded is based on the extraordinary exam weighted 70% and assignments/practicals weighted 30%.
